checks: Checked source 443fb78ca8dd4f80 §§9–12 and Appendix A. For interior tent parameters the endpoint sum is continuously differentiable across all mode and support transitions. Full tails give at least one; an empty transition opposite a proper cut has nonzero derivative. Two increasing branches, or a mode against a strict increasing branch on the appropriate side, cannot minimize. Falling and mode-against-falling cases go to the separate falling result. All other minima are strict convex mixed quadratics or the harmless constant P=1.

In the mixed stationary chart the upper-support distance on the falling side is x−T/3. Differentiating gives x=aT/(3D), falling distance VT/(3D), P=1−T²/(9D), and the two mode bounds T≤3D and T≤3D/R. The reflected peak and support formula have 6H=2T+3(R−1) and S₋=R+T/3.

For R≥1, the stronger mode bound is automatic. Fixing R,t gives concavity on each affine roof cell. On both roof lines substituting their linear numerator at fixes affine denominators, so checking T=0 and a=1 suffices. The singular limit is safe by 0<T≤a(1−t). Independently expanded N₁,N₂ from the two frozen formula branches and checked both positivity arguments, including the y≥x² and y≤U domains.

For R<1,H≥0, the area formula is the reciprocal normalization of the menu and the same reflected branches apply. With D≥(1−R)/2 all required denominators are positive; a=0 is infeasible. The cell vertices lie on a=1, T=3D, H=0 or the two stated feasible roof intersections with V=0,R². Independently checked the two N₂ edge values and the two residual-vertex rational expressions. Recomputed the degree-six positive Bernstein vector.

For H≤0 the stationary constraints give the stated triangle, with D≥(1−R)²/2 and T>0 at all vertices. The wide and elementary bounds cover the outer ratio ranges. On each compact cell in the remaining range, a nonzero line direction keeping the one positive affine ratio constant makes its perspective affine and leaves the remaining expression concave. Thus checking the two already covered triangle edges, FG and w=1 is sufficient. Checked monotonicity of U, rectangle containment, and signs of all denominators. The endpoint q=0 values are continuous fixed-tilt limits.

Parsed A,B,C and N₁,N₂ from the exact frozen proof. Independent rational symbolic substitutions reproduced the edge identities and Bernstein minima 8/81, 863692/421875, 111/512, 5/2, 168/125, 138693/100000, 0. Separate source checkers passed 154 exact identities/coefficient checks and 159 printed-table checks. The compact-domain lower bound uses these identities, without treating a finite sample as a proof.

For degenerate facet modes, the kites and Minkowski averages converge in Hausdorff distance and each fixed cap area converges since polygon boundaries and the cutting line have zero area. At the identical one-sided tents R=1,p=q=0,α=0 all three masses are exactly 4/9.

dependencies.hypotheses: The exact symmetric kites are the body data in this theorem. After any swap and determinant-one normalization its slope-order and cap formulas supply m,Q and the reflected case on each of the listed domains. Pending separate same-wave approval.
Used at two falling cuts, a mode against a falling cut, and their feasible limits, and for R≤2/9 after reversing the width order (reciprocal ratio ≥9/2). Pending separate same-wave approval.
The ordinary area centroid of each specified full-dimensional planar body is the metronoid point at mass equal to its full area. At d=2 its closed cap bound is 4/9 of that area.

The two zero caps are nonempty compact convex planar sets of area at least 4/9. Their arithmetic Minkowski average lies in the middle zero cap, and planar Brunn–Minkowski gives that same area lower bound.
dependencies.reference: Brunn–Minkowski, Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski Inequality, Theorem 4.1

overlap.comparison: Reduces the whole-cap functional for arbitrary centered profiles to profiles of at most six pieces, but does not establish the sharp 4/3 bound on the subclass of pairs of triangle tents.
Its single-law paired-tail bound covers identical endpoint laws, but not differing tent modes and widths with the actual midpoint contribution.

readability: The width ratio R is normalized after selecting which tent rises at the candidate minimizer, so it can be less than one. The variables a and V are the rise fraction and the scaled fall fraction, while A,B,C in the last branch name polynomials.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The fixed-tilt inequality follows from an exhaustive minimizing-state reduction, both stationary-branch sign cases, and exact rational certificates on the remaining negative-peak edges.
